newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Labour-force figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics yesterday reveal a moving economy with increased jobs growth. Job creation during January was stronger than expected with employment levels 1.4 per cent higher than a year earlier. The latest Economic Roundup from the Federal Treasury also suggests that the economy is on track to meet the Government's target of 3.5 per cent growth for this financial year. Page 1.

The person at the centre of the current Federal Government political furore, Civil Aviation Safety Authority board member Gabi Hollows, said she had grave doubts about Australian aviation safety if the Transport Minister, John Sharp, and his "friends" succeeded in replacing members from the current CASA board. Page 5.

The collapse of the controversial Australian and New Zealand maritime union "accord" which restricted competition in trans-Tasman shipping has been confirmed with a New Zealand shipping union accepting plans a new venture which seeks to promote the use of foreign vessels in the cargo route. Page 3.

In terms of air passage, the New Zealand Government has revived talks with Australia on the issue of international air passage. It is understood that a high level New Zealand delegation, comprising of industry and government, is pushing for Australia to further open up its aviation market with additional rights for Air New Zealand to fly via Australia to Asia and the US. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has placed his credibility on the line yesterday when he unequivocally backed Transport Minister, John Sharp, against allegations of misconduct linked to pressuring members of the board of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority to resign. However, the Prime Minister's strategy came under threat last night when the person at the centre of the political furore, Gabi Hollows, challenged Sharp's motives. Page 1.

Under a package of recommendations released by a federal parliamentary committee, the recording industry's code of practice could be modified to place a ban on the sale of songs which promote suicide. The reforms are part of a move to curb violence in themedia, but it may result in some music by popular bands from Nirvana to the Beatles being banned. Page 1.

Results from a survey of 3000 doctors reveal almost 30 per cent of Australian deaths follows an explicit medical decision intended to hasten a patients death. The estimate has led to claims that Australia has a higher rate of passive-euthanasia than The Netherlands, where doctors are not prosecuted for assisting death under some circumstances. Page 1.

Australia's unemployment rate remained stable at 8.6 per cent for January with jobs growth increasing by over 38,000 last month - the highest figure since November 1995. However the Federal Government refused to commit itself to a timetable for a turnaround in unemployment. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Police Royal Commission has heard that senior bureaucrats in the NSW Education Department remained silent for 20 years over a teacher's alleged sexual abuse of schoolgirls as young as 13. In the past two days the commission has been told of a number of senior department officials who knew that a male teacher was sexually active with 15-year-old girls and abusing others. Page 1.

US health company Columbia/HCA is poised to enter the Australian health care market in a move that will encourage the privatisation of public hospitals and the US-style "managed care" system will be speeded up with companies competing to offer cheaper serices and lower costs. Page 1.

The Australian Meat and Livestock Corp moved quickly yesterday into damage control mode over possible consumer alarm at Victoria's anthrax outbreak and the infection of 26 meat workers with Q fever at a plant in southern NSW. The AMLC also called on the Government for the first time to protect and preserve Australia's quarantine programs. Page 2.

Almost a third of deaths in Australia had followed an explicit medical decision to hasten the patient's death, a landmark study of euthanasia has found. The findings will be published in the Medical Journal of Australia next week. Page 3.
THE AGE

In the annual Report on Government Service Provision 1997, Victoria came out on top as one of the safest states with low assault and break-in rates, but it was also revealed that it ran one of the leanest education systems, after slashing spending for eac student by 12 per cent between 1993 and 1995. Page A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett and his deputy, Pat McNamara, appear to be polarised on the controversial BHP plan for a gas rig to be installed 14 kilometres from one of the state's most famous coastal landmarks - the Twelve Apostles. Kennett backed the projects, citing jobs and wealth, however McNamara appeared cautious, claiming an environmental impact study would determine the project's suitability. Page A1.

According to recommendations by a Federal Government committee, television networks should face on-the-spot fines of up to A$100,000 if caught showing excessive violence and the films they plan to screen should be given random checks for violence. The comittee also recommended a new range of classifications should be imposed, requiring the networks to label films according to the severity of the violence. Page A1.

Prime Minister John Howard, yesterday launched an offensive, claiming he wanted to join his Transport Minister in making the skies safer by removing board members from the Civil Aviation Safety Authority. Meanwhile the Federal Opposition demanded a judicil inquiry into Sharp's attempts to secure the resignation of CASA board members, including Gabi Hollows. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
